chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him)

That Ali (peace be upon him) was visited by a man who said: 'My female slave has breastfed my child, and I intend to sell her.' He said: 'Take her by the hand and say: Who will buy from me the mother of my child?'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling a female slave who breastfed her master's child?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructed the man to sell his female slave who had breastfed his child by keeping her attached as an 'Umm Walad' (mother of the child). This ruling establishes that upon the master's death, the slave becomes free, and thus she should not be sold separately from the child to preserve her status. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration highlights the legal mechanism of 'tamassuk' (attachment), ensuring the slave's manumission is secured through the transaction rather than waiting for the master's death, while maintaining the breastfeeding bond that prohibits marriage.
